- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to next forecast.  
- If model forecast is significantly above true (e.g., >5% deviation) and sentiment is neutral or mixed, assume mean reversion; reduce forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early correction (first 5–7 days) after a spike, model often misses it; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% in first 3–5 days of forecast horizon.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.00 → +0.67), model may be overfitting; apply a 1–2% smoothing filter to avoid excessive volatility.
